notes: 'full of the spirit': the 'of' and the 'the' are supplied on the complement noun רוּחַ, which stands with no preposition of its own (rules 15, 33); the competing reading would treat 'of' as the adjective's English valency on the analogy of rule 44's verb clause.
כַּאֲשֶׁר is fused as 'as', headed on the governing morpheme standing first (rule 23).
Both object markers (s011, s028) are unrepresented, the ASV writing 'his hands' and 'Moses' bare (rule 16).
